# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.1.17.215 |
| MAC address | 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ |
| AD/workgroup domain | bluemoontuesday.com (NetBIOS: BLUEMOONTUESDAY) |
| Logged-in Windows user | shutchenson (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.17.215) |
| Domain controller | WIN-GSH54QLW48D.bluemoontuesday.com (10.1.17.2) |

## 2. Malware Family / Attribution

**Behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No AV/IDS alert file was present in the evidence directory (only the pcap), so this is traffic-based attribution, not a hash/YARA match.

The infection is a **ClickFix-style fake-CAPTCHA / "verify you are human" social-engineering lure** that tricks the user into pasting a malicious command into the Windows Run dialog. That command launches a hidden PowerShell downloader, which fetches a second-stage obfuscated PowerShell backdoor. The backdoor beacons to its C2 using the infected machine's disk volume serial number as a bot ID, and on command pulls down a **trojanized/hijacked TeamViewer package** (legitimate TeamViewer.exe + resource DLL, plus a malicious loader DLL that hooks `CreateMutexA`/`CreateProcessA` to run TeamViewer silently and invisibly) — giving the attacker covert full remote-desktop control ("Hidden TeamViewer" RAT technique).

Infection chain observed in the capture, in order:
1. `t=38.19s` — DNS query for `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (fake Google Authenticator/verification lure page).
2. `t=38.86s` — DNS query for `authenticatoor.org` (ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA JS widget, loaded 82.221.136.26).
3. `t=52.29s` — DNS query for `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (compromised WordPress-style site hosting/redirecting the lure, 217.70.186.109).
4. `t=60.30s` — First contact to C2 `5.252.153.241:80`, `GET /api/file/get-file/264872` → returns a VBScript "HTA component" that launches `powershell -WindowStyle Hidden` while opening a decoy tab to `azure.microsoft.com`/`teams.microsoft.com` for cover.
5. `t=62.15s` — `GET /api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` → Base64/UTF8-obfuscated PowerShell that decodes to a beacon loop: reads C: volume serial, converts to decimal (matches the recurring `/1517096937` beacon path seen for the rest of the capture), then loops `DownloadString(http://5.252.153.241/<serial>)` → `Invoke-Expression` every 5 seconds — a classic fileless PowerShell RAT/C2 loop.
6. `t≈125-129s` — C2 commands (`k=` status pings) trigger download of `TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV` (malicious hooking DLL), and `pas.ps1` (persistence copy of the same backdoor, confirmed by the beacon message `"startup shortcut created; status = success"`).
7. `t≈611-620s onward` — Outbound TeamViewer "DynGate" protocol traffic to `master16.teamviewer.com` (185.188.32.26) — the hijacked TeamViewer instance phoning home to legitimate TeamViewer relay infrastructure while running hidden.
8. `t=889.6s` onward — Sustained ~1720-second, 10 MB bulk raw-TCP session to `45.125.66.32:2917` (no TLS/HTTP framing) — consistent with the resulting interactive remote-control/screen-data channel.
9. Recurring C2 status beacon: `k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started`.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Malicious domains
| Domain | Resolved IP | Role |
|---|---|---|
| google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net | 104.21.64.1 (Cloudflare) | Fake Google-Authenticator phishing/lure page |
| authenticatoor.org | 82.221.136.26 | ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA delivery widget |
| appointedtimeagriculture.com | 217.70.186.109 | Compromised/redirector site in lure chain |

### C2 / malicious network endpoints
| IP:Port | Purpose |
|---|---|
| 5.252.153.241:80 | Primary C2 — payload staging (`get-file` API) and PowerShell beacon/tasking loop |
| 45.125.66.32:2917 | Post-compromise bulk data channel (remote-control/screen traffic) |
| 45.125.66.252:443 | Secondary TLS session to same attacker /24 as above |
| 185.188.32.26 (master16.teamviewer.com, port 443, DynGate protocol) | Hijacked TeamViewer relay traffic (legitimate TeamViewer infrastructure abused for covert remote access) |

### Malicious URLs
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` — VBScript/HTA dropper stage
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` — obfuscated PowerShell backdoor/beacon loop
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` — persistence copy of backdoor
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer` — legitimate TeamViewer binary (abused)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr` — TeamViewer resource DLL (abused)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV` — malicious mutex/process-hooking loader DLL
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` — recurring beacon/tasking poll (bot ID = victim's disk volume serial in decimal)

### Transferred files and SHA256 hashes
| File | Type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 264872 | VBScript/HTA dropper (417 B) | c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103 |
| 29842.ps1 | Obfuscated PowerShell backdoor | b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded |
| pas.ps1 | Obfuscated PowerShell (persistence copy) | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |
| TeamViewer | Legitimate TeamViewer.exe (abused) | 904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e |
| Teamviewer_Resource_fr | TeamViewer resource DLL (abused) | 9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192 |
| TV | Malicious loader DLL (hooks CreateMutexA/CreateProcessA) | 3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7 |

## 4. Summary
DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, user shutchenson) was compromised via a ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA lure chain (burleson-appliance.net → authenticatoor.org → appointedtimeagriculture.com), leading to execution of a hidden PowerShell backdoor with C2 at 5.252.153.241. The backdoor established a persistent beacon (bot ID = disk volume serial) and, on C2 command, deployed a hijacked/hidden TeamViewer instance for full interactive remote control, with subsequent large-volume remote-control traffic to 45.125.66.32:2917 and legitimate TeamViewer relay infrastructure (185.188.32.26) abused for covert connectivity.
